# llmwiki

> A single binary that makes Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern scale.

> **Also a library** (`src/lib.rs`). Host crates (e.g. `physis_pro`) link it
> in-process instead of shelling out to the binary:
> `index(wiki_root, incremental)` and `search_bm25(wiki_root, query, top_k)`.
> Build BM25-only with `default-features = false` (no `fastembed`/`usearch`);
> the `semantic` feature adds the vector path. The binary is unaffected.

---

## The Problem

In April 2026, Andrej Karpathy published [llm-wiki.md](https://gist.github.com/karpathy/442a6bf555914893e9891c11519de94f) — a pattern for building personal knowledge bases where an LLM incrementally builds and maintains a persistent wiki instead of re-discovering knowledge from scratch on every query.

The core insight is genuinely good: **compile knowledge once at ingest time, query the compiled wiki forever.**

But there's a structural flaw nobody said plainly enough.

The pattern relies on `index.md` — a markdown file listing every page in the wiki — as the LLM's navigation layer. The LLM reads it first on every query to figure out which pages are relevant, then loads those pages.

This works beautifully up to ~100 pages.

After that, the math breaks:

```
500 pages  →  index.md alone = ~8,000 tokens
             + 5 pages loaded = ~10,000 tokens
             = 18,000 tokens consumed before reasoning starts
             = context window half gone before the LLM says a word
```

The wiki becomes more valuable as it grows. The index makes it less usable as it grows. **The thing that was supposed to help becomes the bottleneck.**

Karpathy himself acknowledged this:

> *"Personally I prefer to ingest sources one at a time and stay involved."*

Which is fine for a personal research project. Not fine if you want to index 10,000 internal documents, a legal corpus, a codebase, or anything that actually matters at scale.

---

## The Fix

Replace `index.md` with a real search engine.

Not Elasticsearch. Not a vector database service. Not a Python stack with 40 dependencies.

**A single Rust binary that runs on your machine, offline, forever.**

```
llmwiki search "temperature effect on photosynthesis"

[1] bio/photosynthesis.md  (score: 0.94)
    How plants convert light to glucose via chlorophyll.
    C3/C4/CAM variants. Temperature sensitivity 25-35°C.
    → match at: L67 "temperature" · L89 "thermal stress"

[2] bio/enzymes/rubisco.md  (score: 0.87)
    CO₂ fixation enzyme. Rate peaks at 30°C, inhibited above 40°C.
    → match at: L23 "temperature"

[3] bio/chloroplast.md  (score: 0.71)
    Organelle where photosynthesis occurs. Membrane destabilizes above 42°C.
    → match at: L12 "thermal"
```

The LLM gets 3 snippets (~150 tokens) and decides what to read in full. Context window stays free for reasoning.

**10,000 pages or 100 pages — the LLM always sees the same number of tokens.**

---

## How It Works

Every wiki page has a frontmatter block at the top:

```markdown
---
title: Photosynthesis
description: How plants convert light to glucose via chlorophyll. C3/C4/CAM variants. Temperature sensitivity 25-35°C.
confidence: 0.94
updated: 2026-04-20
---

# Photosynthesis

Full content here...
```

The `description` field is what appears in search results — like a Google snippet. The LLM writes this when it creates or updates a page. Dense, precise, under 200 characters.

`llmwiki` indexes these files and exposes three things:

**1. Keyword search** via Tantivy (BM25, same engine behind many production search systems)

**2. Semantic search** via fastembed + usearch (local embeddings, no API, no cloud)

**3. Hybrid search** — both merged via Reciprocal Rank Fusion, best of both worlds

The index lives in `.index/` — a generated cache that belongs in `.gitignore`. The markdown files are the source of truth. Human-readable, git-diffable, Obsidian-compatible.

---

## Architecture

```
your-wiki/
  bio/
    photosynthesis.md     ← source of truth, plain markdown
    cellular-respiration.md
  .index/                 ← generated by llmwiki, never committed
    tantivy/              ← keyword index, BM25
    vectors.usearch       ← semantic index, cosine similarity
    meta.jsonl            ← page metadata, descriptions, titles
    checksum.json         ← for incremental reindex
```

The separation matters:

```
Human layer:   .md files  →  Obsidian, VSCode, git, any editor
Search layer:  .index/    →  llmwiki, invisible to human workflow
LLM layer:     MCP tools  →  search(), read(), write()
```

LLM writes pages. Rust indexes them. Human reads in Obsidian. No one steps on anyone else.

---

## MCP Integration

`llmwiki` runs as an MCP server. Claude (or any MCP-compatible agent) gets five tools:

| Tool      | What it does                                           |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `search`  | Keyword, semantic, or hybrid search. Returns snippets. |
| `read`    | Read a page or extract a specific section.             |
| `write`   | Create or update a page. Auto-reindexes on write.      |
| `reindex` | Rebuild the index. Incremental by default.             |
| `list`    | List pages by path or tag.                             |

The LLM never loads `index.md`. It never loads the full wiki. It asks, gets back pointers, decides what to read.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "llmwiki": {
      "command": "llmwiki",
      "args": ["serve", "--wiki-root", "/path/to/your/wiki"]
    }
  }
}
```

---

## Why This Scales

|                         | Karpathy pattern             | llmwiki                      |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Navigation              | Load `index.md` into context | `search()` tool, zero tokens  |
| 100 pages               | ✅ Works well                 | ✅ Works well                  |
| 1,000 pages             | ⚠️ index.md overflows context | ✅ Same performance            |
| 10,000 pages            | ❌ Unusable                   | ✅ Same performance            |
| Token cost per query    | Grows with wiki size         | Constant regardless of size   |
| Contradiction tracking  | Manual lint pass             | `confidence` field + git diff |
| Stale content detection | Periodic review              | `updated` field + git log     |
| Source of truth         | LLM-generated prose          | Plain markdown, human-owned   |

---

## What This Is Good For

The LLM Wiki pattern — and by extension llmwiki — is most valuable for knowledge that **no LLM will ever know from training**:

- Internal codebases and architectural decisions
- Legal corpora with jurisdiction-specific interpretations
- Medical protocols specific to an institution
- Regulatory documents that change frequently
- Competitive intelligence and market data
- Anything your organization has generated that isn't public

For these domains, the knowledge is private, the volume is large, and it changes constantly. RAG re-discovers from scratch on every query. llmwiki compiles once and keeps current.

---

## Philosophy

**Human-first.** Files are plain markdown. Open in Obsidian, VSCode, or `cat`. No lock-in, no proprietary format.

**Git-friendly.** Content lives in `.md` files. `.index/` is in `.gitignore`. `git diff` shows exactly what the LLM changed and when. `git revert` if it did something wrong.

**Offline.** No API keys. No cloud. Tantivy and usearch run on-device. fastembed downloads the embedding model once and caches it locally.

**One binary.** `cargo install llmwiki`. Done.

> *"The wiki is just a git repo of markdown files. You get version history, branching, and collaboration for free."* — Karpathy, llm-wiki.md
>
> We kept that part. We just made the search not fall apart at scale.

---

## Install

```sh
cargo install llmwiki
```

Or from source:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/krakiun/llm-wiki
cd llm-wiki
cargo build --release
```

---

## Quick Start

```sh
cd my-wiki
llmwiki init
llmwiki index
llmwiki search "your query here"
llmwiki serve   # starts MCP server + file watcher
```

## Credits

This project is a direct response to Andrej Karpathy's [llm-wiki.md](https://gist.github.com/karpathy/442a6bf555914893e9891c11519de94f) pattern. The core idea — persistent, compounding knowledge compiled by an LLM — is his. We just solved the retrieval problem that makes it viable at scale.

The inverted index insight, the separation of human layer from search layer, and the single-binary constraint came from thinking hard about what Karpathy's pattern actually needed to work in production.

---

*Built in Rust. Inspired by a gist. Designed for the knowledge that matters most — the kind no model was trained on.*
